newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia expels South African prostitutes.
newsitem.headline: Australia expels South African prostitutes.

text.p: Australia asked seven South African women prostitutes and their pimps to leave the country on Thursday after catching the women "red-handed" with Japanese fishermen in raids near the western port of Fremantle.
Two of the women had already boarded flights back to South Africa by Thursday afternoon, an immigration official told Reuters. The others would follow by Friday morning, he added.
The prostitutes and pimps were detained after immigration and customs officials launched joint raids on Wednesday night on two apartments in Fremantle and one in nearby Perth.
All nine South Africans carried tourist visas which prohibited them from working, immigration and customs official said. The youngest woman was 17, they added.
"They were engaged in paid employment which is in clear breach of their visa conditions," Immigration Department spokesman Jamie McCormack said by telephone from Perth.
"They were involved in servicing crews of Japanese tuna boats....Red-handed is perhaps the way to describe it," he said.

Both immigration and customs authorities, which had placed the crewmen and prostitutes under surveillance, could not explain why the prostitutes travelled to Australia to carry out an occupation as common here as elsewhere.
"They have obviously determined it's worth their while," McCormack said.
Fremantle is busy with up to 20 Japanese fishing boats at any time during the tuna season between October and March, said customs official Astrid Norgard.
